notes: File is a single 13-row CSV ('export') — no header rows, no merged cells, no hidden rows/columns, no formulas, so T0 is an ordinary table starting at row 0 (header_row=0).

Row conflict to settle with the operator: SKU 00470001 and the product name 'SIM neutral 1' each occur twice (12 distinct SKUs over 13 rows), and the Net price column has 13 distinct values including an isolated 9999.0 far outside the 1234.56-1335 range. That duplicated SKU therefore carries two different prices under the same price_list 'standard' with no effective_from/effective_to, which violates the /prices identity keys (/price_list, /effective_from). Operator decision needed: is the second 00470001 row a correction/supersede, a different price list that was not labelled, or a genuine duplicate to keep as a second /prices item (in which case an effective_from value must supply the distinguishing key)?

Unresolved/absent optional data: no effective_from, effective_to, brand, barcode, category, description, status, inventory or promotion columns exist anywhere in the file. Currency MYR and VAT rate 5% are taken from source columns and are not converted or re-rates; the schema defaults (THB, 0.07) are not applied because explicit per-row evidence exists.
No other sheets or files are present, so no table can be classified as inventory, promotions or categories.

Kept SKU as a text cast (leading zeros preserved), currency MYR read from the source column (schema default THB not applied, no FX conversion), sales unit PCS via unit_normalize, and the explicit 5% VAT rate / 'No' tax-included flag from source.

/unit/pack_size, /brand, /barcode, /category, /description, /prices/*/effective_from, /prices/*/effective_to, /inventory and /promotions have no source column anywhere in the file and stay unmapped rather than invented.
/status is filled only by the contract default 'active'; the file has no status column.
